transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Dora, a clinical conversational agent. I'm here to answer any questions you may have about your cataract surgery or recovery. Do you have any questions for me?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for taking my call. I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should avoid any exercise for 1 week after surgery, but you can then go back to light exercise, such as gardening. However, you should avoid strenuous exercise for a month.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Got it, I'll make sure to take it easy with the gardening. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's good to know. I've been holding off just in case. Another thing I wanted to ask is, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you go outside. However, if you have significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further.
